gorcock: The moor cock, or red grouse. See Grouse. [Prov. Eng.]
goldfish: (a) A small domesticated cyprinoid fish (Carassius auratus); -- so named from its color. It is native of China, and is said to have been introduced into Europe in 1691. It is often kept as an ornament, in small ponds or glass globes. Many varieties are known. Called also golden fish, and golden carp. See Telescope fish, under Telescope.
goodly: 1. Pleasant; agreeable; desirable. We have many goodly days to see. Shak. 2. Of pleasing appearance or character; comely; graceful; as, a goodly person; goodly raiment, houses. The goodliest man of men since born. Milton. 3. Large; considerable; portly; as, a goodly number. Goodly and great he sails behind his link. Dryden.
gobioid: Like, or pertaining to, the goby, or the genus Gobius. -- n. A gobioid fish.
gordiacea: A division of nematoid worms, including the hairworms or hair eels (Gordius and Mermis). See Gordius, and Illustration in Appendix.
gothamist: A wiseacre; a person deficient in wisdom; -- so called from Gotham, in Nottinghamshire, England, noted for some pleasant blunders. Bp. Morton.
goslet: One of several species of pygmy geese, of the genus Nettepus. They are about the size of a teal, and inhabit Africa, India, and Australia.
goulardsextract: An aqueous solution of the subacetate of lead, used as a lotion in cases of inflammation. Goulard's cerate is a cerate containing this extract.
govern: 1. To direct and control, as the actions or conduct of men, either by established laws or by arbitrary will; to regulate by authority. "Fit to govern and rule multitudes." Shak. 2. To regulate; | To exercise authority; to administer the laws; to have the control. Dryden.
goodbye: Farewell; a form of address used at parting. See the last Note under By, prep. Shak.
gormandize: To eat greedily; to swallow voraciously; to feed ravenously or like a glutton. Shak.
goatish: Characteristic of a goat; goatlike. Give your chaste body up to the embraces Of goatish lust. Massinger. -- Goat"ish*ly, adv. -- Goat"ish*ness, n.
gowdnook: The saury pike; -- called also gofnick.
gorcrow: The carrion crow; -- called also gercrow. [Prov. Eng.]
godwit: One of several species of long-billed, wading birds of the genus Limosa, and family Tringidæ. The European black-tailed godwit (Limosa limosa), the American marbled godwit (L. fedoa), the Hudsonian godwit (L. hæmastica), and others, are valued as game birds. Called also godwin.
godlike: Resembling or befitting a god or God; divine; hence, preeminently good; as, godlike virtue. -- God"like`ness, n.
governing: 1. Holding the superiority; prevalent; controlling; as, a governing wind; a governing party in a state. Jay. 2. (Gram.) Requiring a particular case.
gonfalon: 1. The ensign or standard in use by certain princes or states, such as the mediæval republics of Italy, and in more recent times by the pope. 2. A name popularly given to any flag which hangs from a crosspiece or frame instead of from the staff or the mast itself. Standards and gonfalons, 'twixt van and rear, Stream in the air. Milton.
goff: A silly clown. [Prov. Eng.] Halliwell. | A game. See Golf. [Scot.] Halliwell.
gowk: To make a, booby of one); to stupefy. (old) B. Jonson. | 1. The European cuckoo; -- called also gawky. 2. A simpleton; a gawk or gawky.
gorgonize: To have the effect of a Gorgon upon; to turn into stone; to petrify.
goblet: A kind of cup or drinking vessel having a foot or standard, but without a handle. We love not loaded boards and goblets crowned. Denham.
goutwort: A coarse umbelliferous plant of Europe (Ægopodium Podagraria); -- called also bishop's weed, ashweed, and herb gerard.
goutiness: The state of being gouty; gout.
godless: Having, or acknowledging, no God; without reverence for God; impious; wicked. -- God"less*ly, adv. -- God"less*ness, n.
goosefoot: A genus of herbs (Chenopodium) mostly annual weeds; pigweed.
gondola: 1. A long, narrow boat with a high prow and stern, used in the canals of Venice. A gondola is usually propelled by one or two oarsmen who stand facing the prow, or by poling. A gondola for passengers has a small open cabin amidships, for their protection against the sun or rain.
goral: An Indian goat antelope (Nemorhedus goral), resembling the chamois.
gonimous: Pertaining to, or containing, gonidia or gonimia, as that part of a lichen which contains the green or chlorophyll-bearing cells.
gonoph: A pickpocket or thief. [Eng. Slang] Dickens.
gooroo: A spiritual teacher, guide, or confessor amoung the Hindoos. Malcom.
golgotha: Calvary. See the Note under Calvary.
gownman: One whose professional habit is a gown, as a divine or lawyer, and particularly a member of an English university; hence, a civilian, in distinction from a soldier.
gopherwood: A species of wood used in the construction of Noah's ark. Gen. vi. 14.
goniatite: One of an extinct genus of fossil cephalopods, allied to the Ammonites. The earliest forms are found in the Devonian formation, the latest, in the Triassic.
goliard: A buffoon in the Middle Ages, who attended rich men's tables to make sport for the guests by ribald stories and songs.
godmother: A woman who becomes sponsor for a child in baptism. See Godfather
godhead: 1. Godship; deity; divinity; divine nature or essence; godhood. 2. The Deity; God; the Supreme Being. The imperial throne Of Godhead, fixed for ever. Milton. 3. A god or goddess; a divinity. (old) Adoring first the genius of the place, The nymphs and native godheads yet unknown. Dryden.
goggleeyed: Having prominent and distorted or rolling eyes. Ascham.
golden: 1. Made of gold; consisting of gold. 2. Having the color of gold; as, the golden grain. 3. Very precious; highly valuable; excellent; eminently auspicious; as, golden opinions. Golden age. (a) The fabulous age of primeval simplicity and purity of manners in rural employments, followed by the silver, bronze, and iron ages. Dryden. (b) (Roman Literature) The best part (B. C.
goosewinged: (a) Having a "goosewing." (b) Said of a fore-and-aft rigged vessel with foresail set on one side and mainsail on the other; wing and wing.
gomuti: A black, fibrous substance resembling horsehair, obtained from the leafstalks of two kinds of palms, Metroxylon Sagu, and Arenga saccharifera, of the Indian islands. It is used for making cordage. Called also ejoo.
goodwife: The mistress of a house. (old) Robynson (More's Utopia).
gonimia: Bluish green granules which occur in certain lichens, as Collema, Peltigera, etc., and which replace the more usual gonidia.
gongorism: An affected elegance or euphuism of style, for which the Spanish poet Gongora y Argote (1561-1627), among others of his time, was noted. Gongorism, that curious disease of euphuism, that broke out simultaneously in Italy, England, and Spain. The Critic. The Renaissance riots itself away in Marinism, Gongorism, Euphuism, and the affectations of the Hôtel Rambouillet. J. A.
gobbing: (a) The refuse thrown back into the excavation after removing the coal. It is called also gob stuff. Brande & C. (b) The process of packing with waste rock; stowing.
goth: 1. (Ethnol.) One of an ancient Teutonic race, who dwelt between the Elbe and the Vistula in the early part of the Christian era, and who overran and took an important part in subverting the Roman empire.
gonochorism: (a) Separation of the sexes in different individuals; -- opposed to hermaphroditism. (b) In ontogony, differentiation of male and female individuals from embryos having the same rudimentary sexual organs. (c) In phylogeny, the evolution of distinct sexes in species previously hermaphrodite or sexless.
gomarite: One of the followers of Francis Gomar or Gomarus, a Dutch disciple of Calvin in the 17th century, who strongly opposed the Arminians.
gobemouche: Literally, a fly swallower; hence, once who keeps his mouth open; a boor; a silly and credulous person.
gonfalonier: He who bears the gonfalon; a standard bearer; as: (a) An officer at Rome who bears the standard of the Church. (b) The chief magistrate of any one of several republics in mediæveal Italy. (c) A Turkish general, and standard keeper.
gomarist: One of the followers of Francis Gomar or Gomarus, a Dutch disciple of Calvin in the 17th century, who strongly opposed the Arminians.
golding: A conspicuous yellow flower, commonly the corn marigold (Chrysanthemum segetum). [This word is variously corrupted into gouland, gools, gowan, etc.]
goodman: 1. A familiar appellation of civility, equivalent to "My friend", "Good sir", "Mister;" -- sometimes used ironically. (old) With you, goodman boy, an you please. Shak. 2. A husband; the master of a house or family; -- often used in speaking familiarly. (old) Chaucer. Say ye to the goodman of the house, . . . Where is the guest-chamber Mark xiv. 14.
gougeshell: A sharp-edged, tubular, marine shell, of the genus Vermetus; also, the pinna. See Vermetus.
gossip: 1. A sponsor; a godfather or a godmother. Should a great lady that was invited to be a gossip, in her place send her kitchen maid, 't would be ill taken. Selden. 2. A friend or comrade; a companion; | To stand sponsor to. (old) Shak.
goodtempered: Having a good temper; not easily vexed. See Good-natured.
goolde: An old English name of some yellow flower, -- the marigold (Calendula), according to Dr. Prior, but in Chaucer perhaps the turnsole.
gonococcus: A vegetable microörganism of the genus Micrococcus, occurring in the secretion in gonorrhea. It is believed by some to constitute the cause of this disease.
gourmand: A greedy or ravenous eater; a glutton. See Gormand. That great gourmand, fat Apicius B. Jonson.
governess: A female governor; a woman invested with authority to control and direct; especially, one intrusted with the care and instruction of children, -- usually in their homes.
goody: 1. A bonbon, cake, or the like; -- usually in the pl. [Colloq.] 2. (Zoöl.) An American fish; the lafayette or spot. | Goodwife; -- a low term of civility or sport.
goltschut: 1. A small ingot of gold. 2. A silver ingot, used in Japan as money.
godeyear: The venereal disease; -- often used as a mild oath. (old) Shak.
goby: A passing without notice; intentional neglect; thrusting away; a shifting off; adieu; as, to give a proposal the go-by. Some songs to which we have given the go-by. Prof. Wilson.
godroon: An ornament produced by notching or carving a rounded molding.
goddess: 1. A female god; a divinity, or deity, of the female sex. When the daughter of Jupiter presented herself among a crowd of goddesses, she was distinguished by her graceful stature and superior beauty. Addison. 2. A woman of superior charms or excellence.
gorilla: A large, arboreal, anthropoid ape of West Africa. It is larger than a man, and is remarkable for its massive skeleton and powerful muscles, which give it enormous strength. In some respects its anatomy, more than that of any other ape, except the chimpanzee, resembles that of man.
goshawk: Any large hawk of the genus Astur, of which many species and varieties are known. The European (Astur palumbarius) and the American (A. atricapillus) are the best known species. They are noted for their powerful flight, activity, and courage. The Australian goshawk (A. Novæ-Hollandiæ) is pure white.
goosewing: One of the clews or lower corners of a course or a topsail when the middle part or the rest of the sail is furled.
godliness: Careful observance of, or conformity to, the laws of God; the state or quality of being godly; piety. Godliness is profitable unto all things. 1 Tim. iv. 8.
gorm: Axle grease. See Gome. [Prov. Eng.] | To daub, as the hands or clothing, with gorm; to daub with anything sticky. [Prov. Eng.]
goldenly: In golden terms or a golden manner; splendidly; delightfully. (old) Shak.
gonozooid: A sexual zooid, or medusoid bud of a hydroid; a gonophore. See Hydroidea, and Illust. of Campanularian.
gonoblastid: A reproductive bud of a hydroid; a simple gonophore.
gossiprede: The relationship between a person and his sponsors. (old)
gonys: The keel or lower outline of a bird's bill, so far as the mandibular rami are united.
goa: A species of antelope (Procapra picticauda), inhabiting Thibet.
governor: 1. One who governs; especially, one who is invested with the supreme executive authority in a State; a chief ruler or magistrate; as, the governor of Pennsylvania. "The governor of the town." Shak. 2. One who has the care or guardianship of a young man; a tutor; a guardian. 3. (Naut.) A pilot; a steersman. 4.
gossat: A small British marine fish (Motella tricirrata); -- called also whistler and three-bearded rockling. [Prov. Eng.]
gorgoneion: A mask carved in imitation of a Gorgon's head. Elmes.
goodnow: An exclamation of wonder, surprise, or entreaty. (old) Shak.
goatee: A part of a man's beard on the chin or lower lip which is allowed to grow, and trimmed so as to resemble the beard of a goat.
governableness: The quality of being governable; manageableness.
gonotheca: A capsule developed on certain hydroids (Thecaphora), inclosing the blastostyle upon which the medusoid buds or gonophores are developed; -- called also gonangium, and teleophore. See Hydroidea, and Illust. of Campanularian.
goose: 1. Any large web-footen bird of the subfamily Anserinæ, and belonging to Anser, Branta, Chen, and several allied genera. See Anseres. Note: The common domestic goose is believed to have been derived from the European graylag goose (Anser anser). The bean goose (A.
gothic: 1. Pertaining to the Goths; as, Gothic customs; also, rude; barbarous. 2. (Arch.) Of or pertaining to a style of architecture with pointed arches, steep roofs, windows large in proportion to the wall… | 1. The language of the Goths; especially, the language of that part of the Visigoths who settled in Moesia in the 4th century. See Goth. Note: Bishop Ulfilas or Walfila translated most of the Bible…
goety: Invocation of evil spirits; witchcraft. (old) Hallywell.
gote: A channel for water. [Prov. Eng.] Crose.
goatskin: The skin of a goat, or leather made from it. -- a. Made of the skin of a goat.
goosery: 1. A place for keeping geese. 2. The characteristics or actions of a goose; silliness. The finical goosery of your neat sermon actor. Milton.
gordius: A genus of long, slender, nematoid worms, parasitic in insects until near maturity, when they leave the insect, and live in water, in which they deposit their eggs; -- called also hair eel, hairworm, and hair snake, from the absurd, but common and widely diffused, notion that they are metamorphosed horsehairs.
goodhumored: Having a cheerful spirit and demeanor; good-tempered. See Good- natured.
gopher: 1. One of several North American burrowing rodents of the genera Geomys and Thomomys, of the family Geomyidæ; -- called also pocket gopher and pouched rat. See Pocket gopher, and Tucan. Note: The name was originally given by French settlers to many burrowing rodents, from their honeycombing the earth. 2.
gobline: One of the ropes or chains serving as stays for the dolphin striker or the bowsprit; -- called also gobrope and gaubline.
gooseegg: In games, a zero; a score or record of naught; -- so named in allusion to the egglike outline of the zero sign 0. Called also duck egg. [Slang]
gonocalyx: The bell of a sessile gonozooid.
gossamer: 1. A fine, filmy substance, like cobwebs, floating in the air, in calm, clear weather, especially in autumn. It is seen in stubble fields and on furze or low bushes, and is formed by small spiders. 2. Any very thin gauzelike fabric; also, a thin waterproof stuff. 3. An outer garment, made of waterproof gossamer.
goldeneye: A duck (Glaucionetta clangula), found in Northern Europe, Asia, and America. The American variety (var. Americana) is larger. Called whistler, garrot, gowdy, pied widgeon, whiteside, curre, and doucker. Barrow's golden-eye of America (G. Islandica) is less common.
golf: A game played with a small ball and a bat or club crooked at the lower end. He who drives the ball into each of a series of small holes in the ground and brings it into the last hole with the fewest strokes is the winner. [Scot.] Strutt.
gob: 1. A little mass or collection; a small quantity; a mouthful. [Low] L'Estrange. 2. The mouth. [Prov. Eng.or Low] Wright.
gonydial: Pertaining to the gonys of a bird's beak.
gome: The black grease on the axle of a cart or wagon wheel; -- called also gorm. See Gorm. [Prov. Eng.]
goatfish: A fish of the genus Upeneus, inhabiting the Gulf of Mexico. It is allied to the surmullet.
gomer: A conical chamber at the breech of the bore in heavy ordnance, especially in mortars; -- named after the inventor.
godson: A male for whom one has stood sponsor in baptism. See Godfather.
goutweed: A coarse umbelliferous plant of Europe (Ægopodium Podagraria); -- called also bishop's weed, ashweed, and herb gerard.
goodish: Rather good than the contrary; not actually bad; tolerable. Goodish pictures in rich frames. Walpole.
gormand: A greedy or ravenous eater; a luxurious feeder; a gourmand.
goracco: A paste prepared from tobacco, and smoked in hookahs in Western India.
gooseberry: 1. (Bot.) Any thorny shrub of the genus Ribes; also, the edible berries of such shrub. There are several species, of which Ribes Grossularia is the one commonly cultivated. 2. A silly person; a goose cap. Goldsmith. Barbadoes gooseberry, a climbing prickly shrub (Pereskia aculeata) of the West Indies, which bears edible berries resembling gooseberries.
goer: One who, or that which, goes; a runner or walker; as: (a) A foot. (old) Chapman. (b) A horse, considered in reference to his gait; as, a good goer; a safe goer. This antechamber has been filled with comers and goers. Macaulay.
godly: Pious; reverencing God, and his character and laws; obedient to the commands of God from love for, and reverence of, his character; conformed to God's law; devout; righteous; as, a godly life. | Piously; devoutly; righteously. All that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. 2. Tim. iii. 12.
gon: imp. & p. p. of Go. (old) Chaucer.
golde: An old English name of some yellow flower, -- the marigold (Calendula), according to Dr. Prior, but in Chaucer perhaps the turnsole.
godhood: Divine nature or essence; deity; godhead.
gobetween: An intermediate agent; a broker; a procurer; -- usually in a disparaging sense. Shak.
goemin: A complex mixture of several substances extracted from Irish moss.
goddaughter: A female for whom one becomes sponsor at baptism.
gonad: One of the masses of generative tissue primitively alike in both sexes, but giving rise to either an ovary or a testis; a generative gland; a germ gland. Wiedersheim.
goatsucker: One of several species of insectivorous birds, belonging to Caprimulgus and allied genera, esp. the European species (Caprimulgus Europæus); -- so called from the mistaken notion that it sucks goats. The European species is also goat-milker, goat owl, goat chaffer, fern owl, night hawk, nightjar, night churr, churr-owl, gnat hawk, and dorhawk .
gowned: Dressed in a gown; clad. Gowned in pure white, that fitted to the shape. Tennyson.
gonorrheal: Of or pertaining to gonorrhea; as, gonorrheal rheumatism.
gownsman: One whose professional habit is a gown, as a divine or lawyer, and particularly a member of an English university; hence, a civilian, in distinction from a soldier.
god: 1. A being conceived of as possessing supernatural power, and to be propitiated by sacrifice, worship, etc.; a divinity; a deity; an object of worship; an idol. He maketh a god, and worshipeth it. | To treat as a god; to idolize. (old) Shak.
gossipry: 1. Spiritual relationship or affinity; gossiprede; special intimacy. Bale. 2. Idle talk; gossip. Mrs. Browning.
gold: An old English name of some yellow flower, -- the marigold (Calendula), according to Dr. Prior, but in Chaucer perhaps the turnsole. | 1. (Chem.) A metallic element, constituting the most precious metal used as a common commercial medium of exchange. It has a characteristic yellow color, is one of the heaviest substances known…
governance: Exercise of authority; control; government; arrangement. Chaucer. J. H. Newman.
gonorrhoea: A contagious inflammatory disease of the genitourinary tract, affecting especially the urethra and vagina, and characterized by a mucopurulent discharge, pain in urination, and chordee; clap.
goman: A husband; a master of a family. (old)
gorce: A pool of water to keep fish in; a wear. (old)
goggleeye: (a) One of two or more species of American fresh-water fishes of the family Centrarchidæ, esp. Chænobryttus antistius, of Lake Michigan and adjacent waters, and Ambloplites rupestris, of the Great Lakes and Mississippi Valley; -- so called from their prominent eyes. (b) The goggler.
governable: Capable of being governed, or subjected to authority; controllable; manageable; obedient. Locke.
goodliness: Beauty of form; grace; elegance; comeliness. Her goodliness was full of harmony to his eyes. Sir P. Sidney.
goringcloth: A piece of canvas cut obliquely to widen a sail at the foot.
goodhumoredly: With a cheerful spirit; in a cheerful or good-tempered manner.
goodyship: The state or quality of a goody or goodwife [Jocose] Hudibraus.
goitre: An enlargement of the thyroid gland, on the anterior part of the neck; bronchocele. It is frequently associated with cretinism, and is most common in mountainous regions, especially in certain parts of Switzerland.
goniometrical: Pertaining to, or determined by means of, a goniometer; trigonometric.
gowan: 1. The daisy, or mountain daisy. [Scot.] And pu'd the gowans fine. Burns. 2. (Min.) Decomposed granite.
goodness: The quality of being good in any of its various senses; excellence; virtue; kindness; benevolence; as, the goodness of timber, of a soil, of food; goodness of character, of disposition, of conduct, etc.
gory: 1. Covered with gore or clotted blood. Thou canst not say I did it; never shake Thy gory locks at me. Shak. 2. Bloody; murderous. "Gory emulation." Shak.
gothicism: 1. A Gothic idiom. 2. Conformity to the Gothic style of architecture. 3. Rudeness of manners; barbarousness.
gonorrhoeal: Of or pertaining to gonorrhea; as, gonorrheal rheumatism.
gorgoniacea: One of the principal divisions of Alcyonaria, including those forms which have a firm and usually branched axis, covered with a porous crust, or c Note: The axis is commonly horny, but it may be solid and stony (composed of calcium carbonate), as in the red coral of commerce, or it may be in alternating horny and stony joints, as in Isis. See Alcyonaria, Anthozoa, C.
gourdworm: The fluke of sheep. See Fluke.
gourde: A silver dollar; -- so called in Cuba, Hayti, etc. Simmonds.
gourami: A very largo East Indian freshwater fish (Osphromenus gorami), extensively reared in artificial ponds in tropical countries, and highly valued as a food fish. Many unsuccessful efforts have been made to introduce it into Southern Europe. [Written also goramy.]
gomphosis: A form of union or immovable articulation where a hard part is received into the cavity of a bone, as the teeth into the jaws.
gomphiasis: A disease of the teeth, which causes them to loosen and fall out of their sockets.
gore: 1. Dirt; mud. (old) Bp. Fisher. 2. Blood; especially, blood that after effusion has become thick or clotted. Milton. | 1. A wedgeshaped or triangular piece of cloth, canvas, etc., sewed into a garment, sail, etc., to give greater width at a particular part. 2. A small traingular piece of land. Cowell. 3.
goudron: a small fascine or fagot, steeped in wax, pitch, and glue, used in various ways, as for igniting buildings or works, or to light ditches and ramparts. Farrow.
goldin: A conspicuous yellow flower, commonly the corn marigold (Chrysanthemum segetum). [This word is variously corrupted into gouland, gools, gowan, etc.]
goldfinny: One of two or more species of European labroid fishes (Crenilabrus melops, and Ctenolabrus rupestris); -- called also goldsinny, and goldney.
gonidium: A special groove or furrow at one or both angles of the mouth of many Anthozoa. | A component cell of the yellowish green layer in certain lichens.
gorgeous: Imposing through splendid or various colors; showy; fine; magnificent. Cloud-land, gorgeous land. Coleridge. Gogeous as the sun at midsummer. Shak. -- Gor"geous*ly, adv. -- Gor"geous*ness, n.
gonosome: The reproductive zooids of a hydroid colony, collectively.
gowd: Gold; wealth. [Scot.] The man's the gowd for a' that. Burns.
gorse: Furze. See Furze. The common, overgrown with fern, and rough With prickly gorse. Cowper. Gorse bird (Zoöl.), the European linnet; -- called also gorse hatcher. [Prov. Eng.] -- Gorse chat (Zoöl.), the winchat. -- Gorse duck, the corncrake; -- called also grass drake, land drake, and corn drake.
goodby: Farewell; a form of address used at parting. See the last Note under By, prep. Shak.
gorgonzola: A kind of Italian pressed milk cheese; -- so called from a village near Milan.
goniometer: An instrument for measuring angles, especially the angles of crystals, or the inclination of planes. Contact, or Hand, goniometer, a goniometer having two movable arms (ab, cd), between which (at ab) the faces of the crystals are placed. These arms turn about a fixed point, which is the center of the graduated circle or semicircle upon which the angle is read off.
goliathbeetle: Any species of Goliathus, a genus of very large and handsome African beetles.
goodfellowship: companionableness; the spirit and disposition befitting comrades. There's neither honesty, manhood, nor good fellowship in thee. Shak.
goodnatured: Naturally mild in temper; not easily provoked. Syn. -- Good-natured, Good-tempered, Good-humored. Good-natured denotes a disposition to please and be pleased. Good-tempered denotes a habit of mind which is not easily ruffied by provocations or other disturbing influences.
gonorrhea: A contagious inflammatory disease of the genitourinary tract, affecting especially the urethra and vagina, and characterized by a mucopurulent discharge, pain in urination, and chordee; clap.
gowany: Having, abounding in, or decked with, daisies. [Scot.] Sweeter than gowany glens or new-mown hay. Ramsay.
gove: A mow; a rick for hay. (old) Tusser.
goring: A piece of canvas cut obliquely to widen a sail at the foot.
gooserumped: Having the tail set low and buttocks that fall away sharply from the croup; -- said of certain horses.
goldenrod: A tall herb (Solidago Virga-aurea), bearing yellow flowers in a graceful elongated cluster. The name is common to all the species of the genus Solidago. Golden-rod tree (Bot.), a shrub (Bosea Yervamora), a native of the Canary Isles.
gosherd: One who takes care of geese.
government: 1. The act of governing; the exercise of authority; the administration of laws; control; direction; regulation; as, civil, church, or family government. 2. The mode of governing; the system of polity in a state; the established form of law. That free government which we have so dearly purchased, free commonwealth. Milton. 3. The right or power of governing; authority.
goroonshell: A large, handsome, marine, univalve shell (Triton femorale).
gothicize: To make Gothic; to bring back to barbarism.
gondolier: A man who rows a gondola.
gourd: 1. (Bot.) A fleshy, three-celled, many-seeded fruit, as the melon, pumpkin, cucumber, etc., of the order Cucurbitaceæ; and especially the bottle gourd (Lagenaria vulgaris) which occurs in a great… | A silver dollar; -- so called in Cuba, Hayti, etc. Simmonds.
goggler: A carangoid oceanic fish (Trachurops crumenophthalmus), having very large and prominent eyes; -- called also goggle-eye, big-eyed scad, and cicharra.
gossamery: Like gossamer; flimsy. The greatest master of gossamery affectation. De Quincey.
goal: 1. The mark set to bound a race, and to or around which the constestants run, or from which they start to return to it again; the place at which a race or a journey is to end. Part curb their fiery steeds, or shun the goal With rapid wheels. Milton. 2. The final purpose or aim; the end to which a design tends, or which a person aims to reach or attain.
goat: A hollow-horned ruminant of the genus Capra, of several species and varieties, esp. the domestic goat (C. hircus), which is raised for its milk, flesh, and skin. Note: The Cashmere and Angora varieties of the goat have long, silky hair, used in the manufacture of textile fabrics.
gobang: A Japanese game, played on a checkerboard, in which the object of the game is to be the first in placing five pieces, or men, in a row in any direction.
goldcrest: The European golden-crested kinglet (Regulus cristatus, or R. regulus); -- called also golden-crested wren, and golden wren. The name is also sometimes applied to the American golden-crested kinglet. See Kinglet.
gothite: A hydrous oxide of iron, occurring in prismatic crystals, also massive, with a fibrous, reniform, or stalactitic structure. The color varies from yellowish to blackish brown.
goout: A sluice in embankments against the sea, for letting out the land waters, when the tide is out. [Written also gowt.]
gobelin: Pertaining to tapestry produced in the so-called Gobelin works, which have been maintained by the French Government since 1667.
goosander: A species of merganser (M. merganser) of Northern Europe and America; -- called also merganser, dundiver, sawbill, sawneb, shelduck, and sheldrake. See Merganser.
godship: The rank or character of a god; deity; divinity; a god or goddess. O'er hills and dales their godships came. Prior.
gorgelet: A small gorget, as of a humming bird.
go: 1. To pass from one place to another; to be in motion; to be in a state not motionless or at rest; to proced; to advance; to make progress; -- used, in various applications, of the movement of both… | 1. To take, as a share in an enterprise; to undertake or become responsible for; to bear a part in. They to go equal shares in the booty. L'Estrange. 2. To bet or wager; as, I'll go you a shilling.
governorgeneral: A governor who has lieutenant or deputy governors under him; as, the governor general of Canada, of India.
gopherstate: Minnesota; -- a nickname alluding to the abundance of gophers.
gonidial: Pertaining to, or containing, gonidia. | Of or pertaining to the angles of the mouth; as, a gonidial groove of an actinian.
goliardery: The satirical or ribald poetry of the Goliards. Milman.
gossan: Decomposed rock, usually reddish or ferruginous (owing to oxidized pyrites), forming the upper part of a metallic vein.
godild: A corruption of God yield, i. e., God reward or bless. Shak.
goniometry: The art of measuring angles; trigonometry.
gorget: 1. A piece of armor, whether of chain mail or of plate, defending the throat and upper part of the breast, and forming a part of the double breastplate of the 14th century. 2. A piece of plate armor covering the same parts and worn over the buff coat in the 17th century, and without other steel armor. Unfix the gorget's iron clasp. Sir W. Scott. 3.
gonfanon: 1. The ensign or standard in use by certain princes or states, such as the mediæval republics of Italy, and in more recent times by the pope. 2. A name popularly given to any flag which hangs from a crosspiece or frame instead of from the staff or the mast itself. Standards and gonfalons, 'twixt van and rear, Stream in the air. Milton.
godfather: A man who becomes sponsor for a child at baptism, and makes himself a surety for its Christian training and instruction. There shall be for every Male-child to be baptized, when they can be had, two… | To act as godfather to; to take under one's fostering care. Burke.
gobble: 1. To swallow or eat greedily or hastily; to gulp. Supper gobbled up in haste. Swift. 2. To utter (a sound) like a turkey cock. He . . . gobbles out a note of self-approbation. Goldsmith. | 1. To eat greedily. 2. To make a noise like that of a turkey cock. Prior.
gourmet: A connoisseur in eating and drinking; an epicure.
goapowder: A bitter powder (also called araroba) found in the interspaces of the wood of a Brazilian tree (Andira araroba) and used as a medicine. It is the material from which chrysarobin is obtained.
got: imp. & p. p. of Get. See Get.
gordian: 1. Pertaining to Gordius, king of Phrygia, or to a knot tied by him; hence, intricate; complicated; inextricable. Gordian knot, an intricate knot tied by Gordius in the thong which connected the pole of the chariot with the yoke.
gog: Haste; ardent desire to go. (old) Beau. & Fl.
governmental: Pertaining to government; made by government; as, governmental duties.
godevil: (a) A weight which is dropped into a bore, as of an oil well, to explode a cartridge previously lowered. (b) A device, as a loosely fitted plug, which is driven through a pipe by the pressure of the contents behind the plug to clear away obstructions. (c) A rough sled or dray used for dragging logs, hauling stone, etc. [Local, U. S.]
gospeler: 1. One of the four evangelists. Rom. of R. Mark the gospeler was the ghostly son of Peter in baptism. Wyclif. 2. A follower of Wyclif, the first English religious reformer; hence, a Puritan. (old) Latimer. The persecution was carried on against the gospelers with much fierceness by those of the Roman persuasion. Strype. 3.
gossipy: Full of, or given to, gossip.
gormandizer: A greedy, voracious eater; a gormand; a glutton.
gouge: 1. A chisel, with a hollow or semicylindrical blade, for scooping or cutting holes, channels, or grooves, in wood, stone, etc.; a similar instrument, with curved edge, for turning wood. 2. | 1. To scoop out with a gouge. 2. To scoop out, as an eye, with the thumb nail; to force out the eye of (a person) with the thumb. [K S.] Note: A barbarity mentioned by some travelers as formerly…
goitrous: Pertaining to the goiter; affected with the goiter; of the nature of goiter or bronchocele. Let me not be understood as insinuating that the inhabitants in general are either goitrous or idiots. W. Coxe.
gospel: 1. Glad tidings; especially, the good news concerning Christ, the Kingdom of God, and salvation. And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the… | Accordant with, or relating to, the gospel; evangelical; as, gospel righteousness. Bp. Warburton.
godfearing: Having a reverential and loving feeling towards God; religious. A brave good-fearing man. Tennyson.
gown: 1. A loose, flowing upper garment; especially: (a) The ordinary outer dress of a woman; as, a calico or silk gown. (b) The official robe of certain professional men and scholars, as university students and officers, barristers, judges, etc.; hence, the dress of peace; the dress of civil officers, in distinction from military. He Mars deposed, and arms to gowns made yield.
goblinize: To transform into a goblin. Lowell.
goldsmith: 1. An artisan who manufactures vessels and ornaments, etc., of gold. 2. A banker. (old) Note: The goldsmiths of London formerly received money on deposit because they were prepared to keep it safely. Goldsmith beetle (Zoöl.), a large, bright yellow, American beetle (Cotalpa lanigera), of the family Scarabæidæ
goldfinch: (a) A beautiful bright-colored European finch (Carduelis elegans). The name refers to the large patch of yellow on the wings. The front of the head and throat are bright red; the nape, with part of the wings and tail, black; -- called also goldspink, goldie, fool's coat, drawbird, draw-water, thistle finch, and sweet William. (b) The yellow-hammer.
gour: 1. A fire worshiper; a Gheber or Gueber. Tylor. 2. (Zoöl.) See Koulan.
going: 1. The act of moving in any manner; traveling; as, the going is bad. 2. Departure. Milton. 3. Pregnancy; gestation; childbearing. Crew. 4. pl. Course of life; behavior; doings; ways. His eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings. Job xxxiv. 21. Going barrel.
goggle: To roll the eyes; to stare. And wink and goggle like an owl. Hudibras. | Full and rolling, or staring; -- said of the eyes. The long, sallow vissage, the goggle eyes. Sir W. Scott.
gorbelly: A prominent belly; a big-bellied person. (old)
goldenstate: California; -- a nickname alluding to its rich gold deposits.
gouache: A method of painting with opaque colors, which have been ground in water and mingled with a preparation of gum; also, a picture thus painted.
gong: A privy or jakes. (old) Chaucer. Gong farmer, Gong man, a cleaner of privies. (old) | 1. Etym: [Malayan (Jav.) gong.] An instrument, first used in the East, made of an alloy of copper and tin, shaped like a disk with upturned rim, and producing, when struck, a harsh and resounding…
godsend: Something sent by God; an unexpected acquisiton or piece of good fortune.
gout: 1. A drop; a clot or coagulation. On thy blade and dudgeon gouts of blood. Shak. 2. (Med.) A constitutional disease, occurring by paroxysms. It constists in an inflammation of the fibrous and ligamentous parts of the joints, and almost always attacks first the great toe, next the smaller joints, after which, it may attack the greater articulations.
gobstick: 1. (Angling) A stick or device for removing the hook from a fish's gullet. He . . . wrenched out the hook with the short wooden stick he called a "gobstick." Kipling. 2. A spoon. [Prov. Eng. or Slang]
goblin: An evil or mischievous spirit; a playful or malicious elf; a frightful phantom; a gnome. To whom the goblin, full of wrath, replied. Milton.
gorgonian: 1. Pertaining to, or resembling, a Gorgon; terrifying into stone; terrific. The rest his look Bound with Gorgonian rigor not to move. Milton. 2. (Zoöl.) Pertaining to the Gorgoniacea; as, gorgonian coral.
gonophore: 1. (Zoöl.) A sexual zooid produced as a medusoid bud upon a hydroid, sometimes becoming a free hydromedusa, sometimes remaining attached. See Hydroidea, and Illusts. of Athecata, Campanularian, and Gonosome. 2. (Bot.) A lengthened receptacle, bearing the stamens and carpels in a conspicuous manner.
gorgonia: 1. A genus of Gorgoniacea, formerly very extensive, but now restricted to such species as the West Indian sea fan (Gorgonia flabellum), sea plume (G. setosa), and other allied species having a flexible, horny axis. 2. Any slender branched gorgonian.
gothamite: 1. A gothamist. 2. An inhabitant of New York city. [Jocular] Irving.
gorgerin: In some columns, that part of the capital between the termination of the shaft and the annulet of the echinus, or the space between two neck moldings; -- called also neck of the capital, and hypotrachelium. See Illust. of Column.
gobbet: A mouthful; a lump; a small piece. Spenser. [He] had broken the stocks to small gobbets. Wyclif. | To swallow greedily; to swallow in gobbets. [Low] L'Estrange.
goaf: That part of a mine from which the mineral has been partially or wholly removed; the waste left in old workings; -- called also gob . To work the goaf or gob, to remove the pillars of mineral matter previously left to support the roof, and replace them with props. Ure.
goodygoody: Mawkishly or weakly good; exhibiting goodness with silliness. [Colloq.]
godspeed: Success; prosperous journeying; -- a contraction of the phrase, "God speed you." [Written also as two separate words.] Receive him not into house, neither bid him God speed. 2 John 10.
goll: A hand, paw, or claw. (old) Sir P. Sidney. B. Jonson.
gocart: A framework moving on casters, designed to support children while learning to walk.
gossypium: A genus of plants which yield the cotton of the arts. The species are much confused. G. herbaceum is the name given to the common cotton plant, while the long-stapled sea-island cotton is produced by G. Barbadense, a shrubby variety. There are several other kinds besides these.
goffer: To plait, flute, or crimp. See Gauffer. Clarke.
gourdtree: A tree (the Crescentia Cujete, or calabash tree) of the West Indies and Central America.
goethite: A hydrous oxide of iron, occurring in prismatic crystals, also massive, with a fibrous, reniform, or stalactitic structure. The color varies from yellowish to blackish brown.
gosling: 1. A young or unfledged goose. 2. A catkin on nut trees and pines. Bailey.
goldbeating: The art or process of reducing gold to extremely thin leaves, by beating with a hammer. Ure.
gobbler: A turkey cock; a bubbling Jock.
gospelize: 1. To form according to the gospel; as, a command gospelized to us. Milton. 2. To instruct in the gospel; to evangelize; as, to gospelize the savages. Boyle.
goneness: A state of exhaustion; faintness, especially as resulting from hunger. [Colloq. U. S.]
good: 1. Possessing desirable qualities; adapted to answer the end designed; promoting success, welfare, or happiness; serviceable; useful; fit; excellent; admirable; commendable; | 1. That which possesses desirable qualities, promotes success, welfare, or happiness, is serviceable, fit, excellent, kind, benevolent, etc.; -- opposed to evil. There be many that say, Who will show…
goldylocks: A plant of several species of the genus Chrysocoma; -- so called from the tufts of yellow flowers which terminate the stems; also, the Ranunculus auricomus, a kind of buttercup.
gouty: 1. Diseased with, or subject to, the gout; as, a gouty person; a gouty joint. 2. Pertaining to the gout. "Gouty matter." Blackmore. 3. Swollen, as if from gout. Derham. 4. Boggy; as, gouty land. (old) Spenser. Gouty bronchitis, bronchitis arising as a secondary disease during the progress of gout.
gord: An instrument of gaming; a sort of dice. (old) Beau. & Fl.
godchild: One for whom a person becomes sponsor at baptism, and whom he promises to see educated as a Christian; a godson or goddaughter. See Godfather.
goiter: An enlargement of the thyroid gland, on the anterior part of the neck; bronchocele. It is frequently associated with cretinism, and is most common in mountainous regions, especially in certain parts of Switzerland.
gorge: 1. The throat; the gullet; the canal by which food passes to the stomach. Wherewith he gripped her gorge with so great pain. Spenser. Now, how abhorred! . . . my gorge rises at it. Shak. 2. | 1. To swallow; especially, to swallow with greediness, or in large mouthfuls or quantities. The fish has gorged the hook. Johnson. 2. To glut; to fill up to the throat; to satiate.
gorged: 1. Having a gorge or throat. 2. (Her.) Bearing a coronet or ring about the neck. 3. Glutted; fed to the full.
gorgon: 1. (Gr. Myth.) One of three fabled sisters, Stheno, Euryale, and Medusa, with snaky hair and of terrific aspect, the sight of whom turned the beholder to stone. The name is particularly given to… | Like a Gorgon; very ugly or terrific; as, a Gorgon face. Dryden.
goad: A pointed instrument used to urge on a beast; hence, any necessity that urges or stimulates. The daily goad urging him to the daily toil. Macaulay. | To prick; to drive with a goad; hence, to urge forward, or to rouse by anything pungent, severe, irritating, or inflaming; to stimulate. That temptation that doth goad us on. Shak. Syn. -- To urge;
goura: One of several species of large, crested ground pigeons of the genus Goura, inhabiting New Guinea and adjacent islands. The Queen Victoria pigeon (Goura Victoria) and the crowned pigeon (G. coronata) are among the beat known species.
goniometric: Pertaining to, or determined by means of, a goniometer; trigonometric.
